guide.title: Central Texas Barbecue from Lockhart to Llano
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: A barbecue trail out of Austin through Taylor, Elgin, Lexington, Lockhart, Luling, Driftwood and Llano, from century-old meat markets to new pits, with a few places to sleep along the way.
sections: Taylor, Elgin and Lexington · 25 to 55 mi northeast of Austin
Driftwood and Spicewood · 25 to 35 mi west of Austin

places.name: Franklin Barbecue
places.notes: The brisket that set off the modern Austin barbecue boom. The line forms well before opening and the meat often sells out, so plan the morning around it or look into preorders on the official site.

places.name: la Barbecue
places.address: 2401 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
places.notes: An East Austin pit with roots in the Mueller barbecue family of Taylor. Peppery brisket, pork ribs and house sausage, served until it runs out.

places.name: LeRoy and Lewis Barbecue
places.notes: South Austin barbecue that treats the sides and the less familiar cuts as seriously as the brisket. Beef cheeks made its name, and the vegetables get real smoke too.

places.name: InterStellar BBQ
places.address: 12233 Ranch Rd 620 N, Suite 105, Austin, TX 78750
places.notes: A strip-mall counter in Northwest Austin that turns out some of the most precise barbecue in the state. Convenient on the way out toward Llano or Spicewood.

places.name: Louie Mueller Barbecue
places.notes: Run by the same family since the 1940s in a room whose walls have gone dark from decades of smoke. Order at the counter, then take a look at the pits. The big beef rib is the classic order.
places.section: Taylor, Elgin and Lexington · 25 to 55 mi northeast of Austin

places.name: Southside Market & Barbeque
places.notes: Elgin has long been called the sausage capital of Texas, and Southside has been making its hot links since 1882. Eat in the big hall or buy links at the meat counter to take home.
places.section: Taylor, Elgin and Lexington · 25 to 55 mi northeast of Austin

places.name: Snow's BBQ
places.notes: A small-town pit open on Saturday mornings only, famous for its longtime pitmaster Tootsie Tomanetz. Get there early: the line starts at dawn and the meat is often gone by late morning. Check the official site before driving out.
places.section: Taylor, Elgin and Lexington · 25 to 55 mi northeast of Austin

places.name: Kreuz Market
places.notes: A huge barn of a meat market with roots going back to 1900. Order by the pound in the pit room and carry it out on butcher paper. The salt-and-pepper brisket and the house sausage are the classic orders.

places.name: Smitty's Market
places.notes: The original Kreuz building, where you walk through a smoky back hall past open fire pits to order. Even if you only stop for a sausage ring, come for the room.

places.name: Black's Barbecue
places.notes: One family has run these pits since 1932. Known for oversized beef ribs and a long cafeteria line of sides. The walls are covered in old photos.

places.name: Chisholm Trail Bar-B-Q
places.notes: The everyday local spot on the south side of town, cafeteria style with plenty of sides. Easier on the wallet and the clock than the famous names.

places.name: Caldwell County Courthouse
places.notes: An ornate 1890s courthouse at the center of a square lined with shops, coffee and antiques. A good place to walk off lunch between pits.

places.name: Lockhart State Park
places.notes: A small state park just south of town with a creek, short trails, a nine-hole golf course and a compact campground. Reserve sites through Texas Parks and Wildlife.

places.name: City Market
places.notes: Order meat in the glassed-in pit room at the back, then sides and drinks up front. Pork ribs, sausage and the house mustard sauce are the reasons to come.

places.name: Palmetto State Park
places.notes: A few miles south of Luling, dwarf palmettos and swampy trails along the San Marcos River feel nothing like the rest of Central Texas. Has a campground and river paddling.

places.name: The Salt Lick BBQ
places.notes: A big open pit under a stone building on a Hill Country ranch, with family-style platters at picnic tables. More about the setting and the afternoon than the brisket. The Driftwood location is BYOB; check the official site for details.
places.section: Driftwood and Spicewood · 25 to 35 mi west of Austin

places.name: Camp Lucy
places.notes: A ranch resort near Dripping Springs with rooms and cottages under old live oaks, about fifteen minutes from the Salt Lick. The splurge stay on this list.
places.section: Driftwood and Spicewood · 25 to 35 mi west of Austin

places.name: Opie's Barbecue
places.notes: Pick meat straight from the pit outside, Llano style, then grab sides inside. The sweet-and-spicy baby back ribs and tater tot casserole are the usual orders. An easy stop on the way to Llano.
places.section: Driftwood and Spicewood · 25 to 35 mi west of Austin

places.name: Cooper's Old Time Pit Bar-B-Que
places.notes: The original Cooper's. Point at what you want from the open mesquite pits out front, then eat at long communal tables inside. The thick pork chop is the signature, and the beans are free.

places.name: Dabbs Hotel
places.notes: A 1907 railroad hotel in Llano's old railyard district, now a small bed-and-breakfast with six suites and a backyard that runs down to the river. A short walk to the courthouse square.
